claims.statement: Python transport and DNS guards precede delegates, preserve numeric loopback and Unix traffic, and fail caught collection, fixture, body and session denials. Expected-denial scopes acknowledge exactly one real denial and cannot leak acknowledgement to later async work or hide invalid scopes.

Automatic exact-origin browser isolation covers existing and future contexts plus direct API request clients, denies route removal and unsafe context options, and prevents redirects. Actual Chromium negative controls fail teardown with zero loopback-tripwire hits, while permitted local requests and native Fetch Metadata remain usable.

Explicit frozen dependency acquisition creates a clean committed-source image. All backend, frontend, 16 unfiltered browser runners and explicit native acceptance tests execute in fresh inspected non-root network-none targets with no host mounts. A separate read-only collector has only BPF/PERFMON capabilities. Both roles bind the source and immutable image, preserve private namespaces and use exact owned cleanup; strict phase inventory and descendant quiescence precede every audit snapshot.

Native ARM64 cgroup hooks audit network/control attempts before filtering. Typed paired exits require readable query output or live-disabled VMA naming with same-task full-width -EINVAL. ABI/ELF, inherited-FD, io_uring, quiescence and balanced pending counts are mandatory. QEMU qualification requires live native-host identity and observed external/Unix controls, not guest-level audit coverage. Network/filter rejection is unchanged; unknowns, read/state errors and incomplete evidence fail.

limitations: CI remains disabled at the user's request. All reported execution is local; acquisition downloads are explicitly separate from test execution.

The host Python and Node guards are not security sandboxes for arbitrary preloaded plugins, native libraries or ordinary subprocesses. Complete-suite evidence additionally requires the inspected Linux network namespace and qualified native ARM64 target-cgroup observation. No ptrace fallback or foreign kernel-ABI acceptance is provided; QEMU qualification covers actual native host kernel calls, not emulated guest operations handled wholly in userspace.

The separate collector requires exactly BPF/PERFMON capabilities, a supported live BTF hook and source-bound bytecode. Global hook attachment filters the target cgroup before register or user-memory reads. Target user-memory snapshots are not an atomic copy of the kernel's later read; no universal adversarial-memory guarantee is claimed.

Native kernel execution is qualified by an unchanged inherited architecture guard and bounded ELF probes, not by assuming CONFIG_COMPAT is absent. A successful foreign ELF requires a separate native-emulation handshake, stable owned process/executable metadata, native header evidence, every emulator thread's profile and observed translated network controls. The header hash is not whole-binary provenance. No inherited sockets/rings and actual io_uring_setup denial remain mandatory.

The kernel negative controls intentionally attempt the reserved TEST-NET address only after proving that loopback is the sole active interface and all routes remain local. Dormant kernel interfaces must be administratively and operationally down. Browser controls use owned loopback tripwires; Python and Node transport controls use harmless delegates.

Default suites use deterministic mock providers, SQLite and local browser stacks. Optional PostgreSQL remains opt-in and its default skips do not qualify a real database or providers. This is not deployment or adversarial Docker-administrator isolation.

Browser evidence qualifies the explicit IP-datagram-disabled test profile, not stock Chromium networking or UDP, QUIC, WebRTC and ordinary DNS behavior. Backend, frontend and native suites do not install the extra browser policy.
In-memory frontend transport mocks are the repository's existing substitute for MSW. Network denial is independently enforced; no claim is made that MSW is installed.

Each offline suite requires a clean exact commit and one matching acquired image. It refuses missing dependencies/images, unsafe runtime opt-ins, ambiguous identities or source drift; it never acquires dependencies as a verification fallback.
